message.reasoning:
I need to decide on a bid for SHORT_LINE in the auction.

Only p2 remains as an opponent. The current bid for SHORT_LINE is $78, requiring a minimum next bid of $79. I have $546 and p2 has $225. My prior strategy was to mortgage Short Line for $100, so any win under $100 would be profitable if mortgaged before rent survival. Folding now would gift p2 roughly $22 in profit.

A bid of $79 nets $21 after mortgaging. Folding lets p2 gain $22. p2 could use the railroad for rent if they unmortgage B&O, but that would cost $100.

I own Reading and Pennsylvania, both mortgaged. Three railroads would still yield no rent until they are unmortgaged.

The plan is to bid $79 and mortgage immediately. I will drop at $100 or higher.

p2 may continue bidding past $100 for strategic reasons. If they reach $99 and I raise to $100, the mortgage value equals the purchase price, so I would break even but lose cash.

A $100 bid nets zero cash but locks capital poorly; unmortgaging would cost $110. A $99 bid nets just $1 profit yet still blocks the arbitrage. p2 may continue bidding past $100 for strategic reasons, though one railroad yields only $25 in rent.

p2 owns a massive property set: orange with four houses each and dark blue with three houses on Park Place and Boardwalk. Boardwalk at three houses pays $1400, and Park Place at three houses pays $1100. With only $546 cash, landing on either would bankrupt me unless I can raise funds quickly.

I need a cash buffer for Park Place and Boardwalk. My light blue monopoly with four houses on Oriental and three on Vermont and Connecticut could be sold to raise funds if I land there.

The auction strategy is to bid $79, continue to $99, and drop at $100 or higher. Forcing p2 to pay $99 for a $100 mortgage value gives me only one dollar profit. Folding at $78 would gift them $22 instead. Continuing is the correct choice.

I considered bidding more aggressively to drain p2 faster. They have matched every dollar from $1 to $78.

I will stick to one-dollar increments. A larger jump risks overpaying if p2 drops, and they will match every bid up to their limit.
